subject: biology
title: Cells in Action
welcome_lead: Travel through cells doing their everyday jobs and see organisation at work.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure showing how cells work together in real body parts.
final_note: You have seen how cells, tissues and organs cooperate to keep you alive.

walkthroughs.body_html: The cell membrane is selective. It lets oxygen and food in and lets waste out by diffusion. Without it the cell could not control its contents.
A large central vacuole filled with cell sap pushes outward on the cell wall. This pressure keeps plant stems and leaves stiff and upright.
Stomach lining cells form tissue that makes acid and enzymes. The stomach (organ) churns food. The digestive system uses it to break food down.

mcqs.q: What is transported in the phloem of a plant?
options: Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Sugars (mainly sucrose) and other organic compounds, from sources (e.g. leaves) to sinks (e.g. roots, fruits).
Phloem transports water from roots to leaves.
Phloem transports oxygen to all parts of the plant.
Each new DNA molecule contains one original (parental) strand and one newly synthesised strand.
DNA replication produces two identical fully new molecules with no original material.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
One daughter molecule contains both original strands; the other contains both new strands.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.
Phloem transports oxygen to all parts of the plant.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
